title: Greet Function
lesson:
## Functions

Functions let you group reusable code under a name.

### Defining and Calling Functions
```python
def greet(name):
    print(f"Hello, {name}!")

greet("Alice")   # Hello, Alice!
greet("Bob")     # Hello, Bob!
```

### Parameters and Return Values
```python
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

result = add(3, 5)
print(result)   # 8
```

### Default Parameters
```python
def greet(name, greeting="Hello"):
    print(f"{greeting}, {name}!")

greet("Alice")            # Hello, Alice!
greet("Bob", "Hi")        # Hi, Bob!
```

### Scope
```python
x = 10  # global variable

def my_func():
    y = 20  # local variable — only exists inside the function
    print(x)  # can read global
    print(y)  # can read local

my_func()
# print(y)  # Error! y doesn't exist here
```

### Why Use Functions?
- Avoid repeating code (DRY principle)
- Make code easier to test and maintain
- Break complex problems into smaller pieces
